title: n-types are closed under retracts: a retract of an n-type is an n-type
author: The Univalent Foundations Program

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.1.4 at source lines 68-73: if p : X -> Y is a retraction and X is an n-type then Y is an n-type. The author's proof (source lines 75-92) is an induction on n in which the step is a genuine construction: after fixing y, y' : Y one must exhibit the path space y = y' as a retract of s(y) = s(y') (source line 83), and this requires writing down both the section ap s and the retraction t(q) := opp(epsilon_y) `ct` ap p q `ct` epsilon_{y'} (source lines 85-87). The retraction identity is not definitional and is discharged at source line 91 by the naturality of the homotopy epsilon : p o s ~ 1, which is exactly the point where the chosen section and homotopy have to interact.
